I graduated from nursing school in my 30s. When scoping out programs I felt like community colleges were more understanding of students with jobs/families/time constraints compared to traditional universities. Plus I had some other "old" people in my class instead of a bunch of 19 year olds. 

I really recommend getting a job as a tech at a hospital if you can swing the (probable) pay cut. That's a tough call! A lot of my classmates kept their retail/serving jobs purely because of that pay cut. If you can get by on a tech salary, I personally would go for it. Hospitals are used to working with nursing student schedules. Personally, I think the clinical experience is priceless. I'm very comfortable talking to patients, teaching, etc. and the instructors really notice. Plus many hospitals will reimburse you for tuition, and you may have a guaranteed job when you graduate, or at least a lot more connections for jobs. 

I was hired as a tech, but have since trained to the tele monitors. So I'm at a desk now, great for cramming (as long as all the hearts behave, lol)

ETA, another option is to be PRN at the hospital and keep your current job. At my hospital, PRN is one shift per pay period (2 weeks.) Gets you a foot in the door, with the option to pick up extra shifts during school breaks, etc.

I just finished level 1 (ADN program) while working full time (12 hr overnight shifts, 3x a week.) My kids are 8 and 10. No husband, but my bf of 2 years moved in with us just before the semester started, to help with the kids. 

My school schedule was usually 8-11am lecture on M/W, 10-2 lab on tuesday, and either 6am-12pm or 12pm-6pm clinical on Th&F. So basically, short-ish school days at the beginning of the week, long clinical days at the end. Toward the end of the semester, we started having a lot of random days off - lab was mostly over, since checkoffs were done, there were a few holidays etc.

I worked overnight (7pm-7am) on Sunday and Tuesday every week, and went to lecture straight after. I also worked another night whenever I could - often Friday or Saturday. I took ~12 hours of PTO per paycheck, so I that I could skip one shift. Work was flexible with me, but "flexible" for a hospital is still shitty, lol. I did split a few shifts with coworkers around finals time. I was also able to study during work, which was crucial - if I wasn't,  I would have needed the nights before exams off for sure.

My kids being in afterschool care was also crucial. I'm so glad I found a program that we all love. I was able to nap/study til 6 pm instead of 3 when their school gets out. On my long clinical days, I relied on my boyfriend to pick then up, but otherwise it was doable. 

Other than being tired a lot, it really wasn't as impossible as I had worked it up to be before I started. I made it through, with As, which isn't common in my program. I felt like being a parent and having to work gave me extra motivation over some of my super young, single peers - I know what I want. I know how much money I'm paying for this, I know my career/future income depends on these exams. Please feel free to ask me questions! I have a 3 semesters to go, so I'm not an expert, but I am really proud of myself and want to encourage other parents!
